card.title: 151st INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Develop AMPHIBIOUS ASSAULT, EXPANSION or FOR PROSPERITY.
card.flavorText: The 151st Infantry Regiment was part of the Imperial Japanese Army's 53rd Division, which was activated in 1941 and nicknamed the “Peace Division.” Originally raised in Kyoto, the division's troops came from several nearby prefectures. Initially held in reserve, it was deployed to Southeast Asia in late 1943, moving through Taiwan and Saigon before arriving in Burma in May 1944. There, the 53rd Division joined the Japanese 33rd Army in the defense of northern Burma. In June, the 153rd Infantry Regiment was detached and nearly destroyed during the Battle of Imphal. The rest of the division fought bitterly against British Chindit forces near Indaw and later in the battle for Mogaung, suffering 1,600 casualties in that engagement alone. In early 1945, the division was drawn into the fighting around Meiktila and Mandalay. Though some regiments supported other Japanese units, the main force attempted to hold ground near Pyawbwe but was overrun by Allied tanks. The division endured heavy losses again at the Sittang Bend and finally ceased fighting on August 17, 1945, after Japan’s surrender.
